title: Count the Words
statement:
Count the words in a line of text.

## Your function

```
int count_words(const char *s);
```

A word is any run of characters that are not spaces or tabs. Punctuation is
part of whatever word it is attached to.

## Watch out

- Several spaces in a row separate *one* pair of words, not several.
- Leading and trailing spaces do not start a word.
- The empty string, and a string of nothing but spaces, both have no words.
- This is the classic one-variable state machine: remember whether you are
  currently inside a word, and count each time you step into one.

tests.name: spaces only
tests.description: Never entering a word means never counting one.
